# MEMORANDUM

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** [Associate]
**Date:** November 2, 2026
**Re:** Besouth Facade Systems, Inc. / Meideis Glass Fabrication Co.: issues in the supply arrangements affecting the Pellworth sale and Besouth's commercial flexibility

---

## 1. Summary

I reviewed all five files in the matter folder:

- the Glass Supply Agreement dated February 1, 2024 (the **Supply Agreement** or **SA**);
- Statement of Work No. 1 for Calloway Pier Tower dated March 18, 2024 (the **SOW**);
- Amendment No. 1 dated June 15, 2026 (the **Amendment**);
- the Besouth Holdings LLC Parent Guaranty dated October 5, 2026 (the **Guaranty**); and
- Meideis's insurance certificate cover letter dated October 20, 2026.

Three issues matter most. They are listed here in priority order:

1. **The Pellworth sale needs Meideis's consent.** The sale of Besouth Holdings LLC to Pellworth is an indirect Change of Control. Without Meideis's prior written consent, Meideis may terminate the Supply Agreement, and the Calloway Pier Tower SOW with it, on 30 days' notice (SA §§1.1, 16.2, 16.3). Nothing in the folder obtains or waives that consent.
2. **Besouth is already locked into a renewal at higher prices.** The non-renewal deadline under the Amendment passed on or about **August 4, 2026**. Besouth is bound to a 24-month Renewal Term running through January 31, 2029. During that term, prices rise 7%, including Calloway Pier Tower prices for glass delivered from February 1, 2027 (Amendment §§2, 3).
3. **Exclusivity is much broader than the commercial deal.** The Supply Agreement makes Meideis the exclusive source for **all** architectural glass bought by Besouth **and its Affiliates** throughout North America (SA §3.1). That overrides the SOW's project-only exclusivity (SA §18.2). After closing, it may reach Pellworth's portfolio companies. Because of item 2, it now runs through January 2029.

These three issues should be handled together. Meideis will likely treat its consent right as leverage. Besouth should treat the consent request as its chance to negotiate the exclusivity and renewal terms at the same time.

---

## 2. Background facts relied on

| Item | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Effective Date | February 1, 2024 | SA §2.1 |
| Initial Term | Three years from the Effective Date, so ending on or about **January 31, 2027** | SA §2.1 |
| Renewal | Automatic 24-month Renewal Terms unless notice of non-renewal is given at least 180 days before expiry | Amendment §2 (new SA §2.2) |
| Renewal pricing | +7% over prices in effect on the last day of the prior term, including SOW prices | Amendment §3.1 (new SA §7.6) |
| Order of precedence | Amendments, then the Supply Agreement, then any Statement of Work | SA §18.2 |
| SOW exclusivity | IGUs for Calloway Pier Tower, Baltimore, Maryland only | SOW §2.1 |
| Guaranty cap | $4,500,000 plus enforcement costs | Guaranty §3 |
| Governing law and forum | Delaware law; New Castle County courts | SA §§17.2, 18.6 |

---

## 3. Issues, in order of priority

### Issue 1: The Pellworth acquisition is an indirect Change of Control that requires Meideis's prior written consent

**Priority:** Highest. This is a deal issue and it requires a client decision.

**Where it appears:**
- Supply Agreement §1.1, definition of "Change of Control"
- Supply Agreement §§16.1, 16.2 and 16.3
- Parent Guaranty §8.2

**What the documents say:**
- **SA §1.1.** A Change of Control includes any acquisition of more than 50% of the voting equity "of Buyer **or of any direct or indirect parent** of Buyer."
- **SA §16.2.** Any Change of Control of Buyer, "including a Change of Control occurring at the level of any direct or indirect parent of Buyer, **is deemed an assignment** of this Agreement by Buyer and requires Supplier's **prior written consent**." Besouth must also give Meideis written notice of the proposed Change of Control **at least 30 days before completion**.
- **SA §16.3.** If a Change of Control occurs without consent, Meideis may terminate the Supply Agreement **and any or all Statements of Work** on 30 days' written notice. It may do so at any time within 12 months after it learns of the Change of Control.
- **SA §16.1.** Any purported assignment in breach of §16 is void.

**Why it matters:**
- Pellworth is acquiring all of the equity of Besouth Holdings LLC, which directly or indirectly owns all of Besouth (Guaranty Recital D). That is squarely a Change of Control "at the level of any direct or indirect parent." It does not matter that Besouth Facade Systems itself is not being sold, or that its own equity does not change hands.
- If consent is not obtained, Meideis can walk away from Calloway Pier Tower mid-project, on 30 days' notice, at any point for up to a year after closing. Besouth would then have to find replacement IGUs for the remaining floors, with lead times of 6 to 12 weeks (SA §5.2; SOW §5.3). It would face schedule and liquidated-damages exposure under its subcontract with Tidewater Hallcroft. It would also have to requalify the mock-up and the structural silicone compatibility testing.
- At a minimum, Meideis has significant leverage to reprice or extract other concessions.
- **The Guaranty does not solve this.** Guaranty §8.2 contemplates a change of control of Besouth Holdings and confirms that the guaranty survives one. However, it is a document about the Guarantor's own payment obligations. It does not contain, refer to or waive Meideis's consent right under SA §16.2. It also could not do so, because SA §18.3 requires a written amendment signed by both Supply Agreement parties. Meideis's acknowledgment of the Guaranty should not be read as advance consent to the sale.
- The 30-day pre-closing notice requirement in SA §16.2 is a separate obligation. If it is missed, that is a further breach even if consent is later obtained.

**Recommendations:**
1. Make Meideis's written consent to the Change of Control a **closing condition, or at least a required closing deliverable**, under the equity purchase agreement with Pellworth. The consent should cover the Supply Agreement and all Statements of Work, including SOW No. 1.
2. The consent should expressly:
   - waive the §16.3 termination right for this transaction;
   - confirm there is no default; and
   - confirm that the Supply Agreement and SOW No. 1 continue on their current terms.
3. Serve the §16.2 notice under SA §18.1 (hand, overnight courier, or email with courier copy) **at least 30 days before the anticipated closing date**.
4. Diary the separate post-closing notice under Guaranty §8.2, which is due within 10 business days after completion.
5. Use the consent request to raise Issues 2 and 3 with Meideis (see Section 4).

**Client decision or follow-up needed:**
- What is the expected signing and closing timetable? Has Pellworth already identified this consent in diligence?
- Has anyone at Besouth or Holdings already told Meideis about the sale? If so, the 12-month window in §16.3 may already be relevant, and we need to know what was said.
- Is the client willing to approach Meideis now, before signing, or does it prefer to wait until after signing? The answer depends on confidentiality and on the leverage considerations below.

---

### Issue 2: The non-renewal window has closed, and Besouth is locked into a 24-month Renewal Term at a 7% price increase

**Priority:** High. This needs disclosure and a commercial decision.

**Where it appears:**
- Amendment No. 1 §2 (new SA §§2.2 and 2.3) and §3 (new SA §7.6)
- Supply Agreement §2.1
- Parent Guaranty Recital C

**What the documents say:**
- **Initial Term.** The Initial Term runs three years from February 1, 2024, so it ends on or about **January 31, 2027** (SA §2.1).
- **Automatic renewal.** The Amendment provides that the Supply Agreement will "automatically renew for successive renewal terms of 24 months each" unless either party gives written non-renewal notice "**at least 180 days before** expiry of the then-current term" (new SA §2.2).
- **Notice deadline.** Counting 180 days back from January 31, 2027 gives a deadline of **August 4, 2026**. Today is November 2, 2026, so the deadline passed about three months ago.
- **Renewal Term dates.** The first Renewal Term runs from February 1, 2027 to January 31, 2029.
- **Price increase.** From the first day of each Renewal Term, Exhibit B prices **and SOW prices for Products delivered during that Renewal Term** increase by **7%**. Any later PPI adjustments under SA §7.2 compound on the increased prices (new SA §7.6).
- **Confirmation from the Guaranty.** The Guaranty is dated October 5, 2026, after the deadline. Recital C states that the Supply Agreement "will renew for a Renewal Term of 24 months beginning February 1, 2027." That is consistent with no non-renewal notice having been given. The stated reason for the Guaranty is credit support "during the Renewal Term" (Recital E).

**Why it matters:**
- **Besouth cannot now avoid the Renewal Term by giving notice.** Any non-renewal notice served today would only take effect at the end of the Renewal Term (January 31, 2029), and only if served by about August 2028.
- **The Calloway Pier Tower price increase is significant.** Any Calloway Pier Tower glass delivered on or after February 1, 2027 will cost 7% more. For example, IGU-1 rises from $27.75 to about $29.69 per sq. ft. The total SOW volume is roughly 186,000 sq. ft., worth about $5.7 million at current SOW prices. Depending on how much remains to be delivered after January 2027, the increase could run to several hundred thousand dollars. Besouth's subcontract price was presumably set without this increase.
- **The renewal also extends the Issue 3 exclusivity through January 2029.** It does the same for the Guaranty exposure described in Issue 4.
- **This has to be disclosed to Pellworth.** The renewal is a known liability and a known pricing change, and it bears on Pellworth's valuation and on the disclosure schedules.
- **A note on the timing of the Amendment.** The Amendment was signed on June 15, 2026, only about seven weeks before the deadline. It converted an agreement that would otherwise have simply expired (the original SA §2.2 allowed only a mutual extension) into an auto-renewing one with a price escalator. It may be worth asking the client what Besouth understood when it signed. That said, nothing in the documents suggests any basis to unwind the Amendment.

**Ambiguity:**
- "Three years from" February 1, 2024 could be read as ending on February 1, 2027 instead of January 31, 2027. On that reading the deadline moves by one day, to about August 5, 2026.
- Neither reading changes the conclusion. The window closed before the Guaranty was signed, and it is closed now.

**Recommendations:**
1. **Do not advise the client that a non-renewal notice is still available for this cycle. It is not.**
2. Seek a **negotiated release or amendment** from Meideis. Options include:
   - (a) an agreed early termination of the master agreement effective January 31, 2027, with SOW No. 1 carved out under SA §2.5 (as renumbered), so that Calloway Pier Tower continues to completion;
   - (b) a waiver of the §7.6 increase for the remainder of SOW No. 1; or
   - (c) a shorter Renewal Term.

   The best time to seek this is alongside the consent request in Issue 1.
3. **Disclose** the renewal, the 7% increase and the Guaranty to Pellworth in the disclosure schedules. Expect Pellworth to price it in or to ask for a specific indemnity.
4. Calendar the next non-renewal deadline: about **August 4, 2028** for a January 31, 2029 expiry.

**Client decision or follow-up needed:**
- Confirm that no non-renewal notice was in fact served. Please ask the client to search its notice files and Meideis correspondence. The Guaranty recital strongly suggests none was.
- How much Calloway Pier Tower glass is scheduled for delivery after February 1, 2027? We need this to quantify the cost of the increase.
- Can Besouth pass any of the increase through under its subcontract with Tidewater Hallcroft? We have not seen the subcontract.
- Does the client want to stay with Meideis beyond Calloway Pier Tower at all? The answer determines which negotiated outcome to pursue.

---

### Issue 3: Overbroad exclusivity. A North America-wide requirements obligation on all architectural glass binds Besouth and its Affiliates, and it overrides the project-limited SOW

**Priority:** High. This affects Besouth's commercial flexibility and Pellworth's wider portfolio.

**Where it appears:**
- Supply Agreement §3.1
- Supply Agreement §1.1, definition of "Affiliate"
- Supply Agreement §18.2
- SOW §2.1

**What the documents say:**
- **SA §3.1.** During the Term, Besouth "shall, and shall cause its Affiliates to, purchase from Supplier **all of its requirements for architectural glass products throughout North America**." This expressly includes IGUs, laminated, heat-strengthened, tempered, coated and spandrel glass, for any facade application. Besouth and its Affiliates may not buy these products from anyone else.
- **SOW §2.1.** The commercial deal, as reflected in the SOW, is narrower. Meideis is the exclusive source only of "insulated glass units for the Calloway Pier Tower project, Baltimore, Maryland."
- **SA §18.2 order of precedence.** If documents conflict, **Amendments prevail over the Supply Agreement, which prevails over any Statement of Work**. The narrower SOW therefore does not cut back §3.1. Even if one reads the two clauses as consistent rather than conflicting (the SOW simply restates part of a broader obligation), the result is the same: §3.1 stands in full.
- **"Affiliate" definition.** It covers any person that "now **or hereafter**" controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with Besouth.

**Why it matters:**
- **Besouth's other projects.** Besouth cannot source any architectural glass for any other project anywhere in North America from anyone but Meideis. That includes competitively bid jobs and jobs where the owner or architect specifies a different fabricator. Any such purchase is a breach, which exposes Besouth to termination under SA §15.1 after a 30-day cure period, and to damages.
- **Pellworth's portfolio.** After closing, Pellworth, Besouth Holdings and every company under Pellworth's common control will be Besouth's Affiliates. Besouth is obliged to "cause" them to buy all of their architectural glass from Meideis. Besouth cannot actually control those companies, so it would be in breach as soon as any of them buys glass elsewhere. Pellworth will see this as a significant problem.
- **Duration.** Because of the Issue 2 renewal, the obligation now runs to at least January 31, 2029.

**Recommendations:**
1. Amend SA §3.1 so that exclusivity is limited to the scope of each SOW. For now, that means **IGUs for Calloway Pier Tower only**, matching SOW §2.1.
2. **Delete the Affiliate reach entirely.** If Meideis insists on some reach, limit it to Besouth's subsidiaries existing at the date of the amendment, and expressly exclude Pellworth, Besouth Holdings and their other portfolio companies.
3. Bundle this request with the consent request in Issue 1. Because the change has to be made by Amendment, it will prevail under §18.2.
4. Pending the amendment, the client should not make new non-Meideis glass purchases without checking with us first.

**Client decision or follow-up needed:**
- **Has Besouth, or Holdings, bought architectural glass from any other supplier since February 1, 2024?** If so, there may be an existing breach. That would need to be disclosed to Pellworth and factored into negotiations with Meideis.
- Does Besouth currently have other projects in bid or underway that use other glass fabricators?
- Pellworth will need to identify any of its portfolio companies that buy architectural glass.

---

### Issue 4: The Parent Guaranty adds a $4.5 million contingent liability that survives the sale

**Priority:** Medium. This is mainly a disclosure point.

**Where it appears:** Parent Guaranty §§1.2, 3, 4.3, 8.1, 8.2 and 8.3.

**What the documents say and why it matters:**
- **Scope.** Besouth Holdings guarantees all of Besouth's payment obligations to Meideis, up to **$4,500,000** plus enforcement costs (§3).
- **Survives the sale.** The Guaranty continues through a change of control of Holdings (§8.2).
- **Not released by the renewal or price increase.** The Renewal Term and the §7.6 price increase do not release or reduce it (§4.3).
- **Duration.** It runs until the Supply Agreement expires and each SOW then in effect is completed (§8.1). That now means through at least January 2029, and longer if Calloway Pier Tower runs past that date.
- **Consequence for Pellworth.** After closing, Pellworth will own an entity carrying this contingent liability.
- **Limits on the risk.** It is a payment-only guaranty (§2.3). Holdings keeps Besouth's defenses, including good-faith invoice disputes (§4.1). A notice-and-cure step is required before Meideis can make demand (§2.2). The practical risk is therefore tied to Besouth's own payment record.

**Recommendations:**
- Disclose the Guaranty to Pellworth.
- Diary the post-closing §8.2 notice to Meideis, due within 10 business days.
- If Meideis agrees to an early end to the master agreement under Issue 2, ask for the Guaranty to be limited to SOW No. 1 obligations.

**Follow-up:** Is Besouth current on all Meideis invoices, and are any invoices in dispute?

---

### Issue 5: Lower-priority commercial points to note

These do not need immediate action but are worth noting for the client briefing.

**(a) Liability cap and warranty remedies (SA §§9.4 and 11.2).**
- Meideis's liability under a SOW, other than under the indemnities and certain carve-outs, is capped at the amounts paid and payable under that SOW.
- Reimbursement of removal and reinstallation costs for defective glass is subject to the same cap.
- For a unitized curtainwall tower, reinstallation costs can be large. The client should check that this cap lines up with Besouth's own warranty obligations to the GC and the Owner.

**(b) Price adjustments (SA §7.2).**
- Since February 2025, Meideis has been able to adjust prices once per contract year in line with the flat-glass PPI.
- We do not know whether any adjustment has been made. That affects the base on which the 7% increase will be calculated.
- **Follow-up:** Ask the client for any §7.2 price notices it has received.

---

### Item reviewed with no issue found: insurance certificate cover letter (October 20, 2026)

- The letter reports coverage that meets or exceeds each minimum in SA §13.1:
  - CGL of $2M per occurrence and $4M aggregate, including products-completed operations;
  - umbrella of $5M;
  - auto liability of $1M;
  - workers' compensation at statutory limits, and employer's liability of $1M.
- All insurers are rated A- VII or better.
- Besouth and its Affiliates are named as additional insureds on a primary and non-contributory basis, covering ongoing and completed operations, as SA §13.2 requires.
- The letter confirms coverage extends to SOW No. 1.
- **Caveat:** We have only the cover letter, not the enclosed ACORD 25 or the endorsements. The client should confirm that the enclosures match the letter's description.
- **Optional step:** If the Calloway Pier Tower subcontract requires the Owner or GC to be named on a separate project certificate, Besouth can request one through Lehigh Crestmark (letter §4.2).

---

## 4. Suggested approach and items for client decision

**Recommended strategy.** Approach Meideis with a single package that asks for:

1. consent to the Pellworth Change of Control and a waiver of the §16.3 termination right;
2. an Amendment narrowing §3.1 exclusivity to Calloway Pier Tower IGUs and removing the Affiliate reach; and
3. relief from the Renewal Term, or at least from the 7% increase on remaining Calloway Pier Tower deliveries.

Meideis's consent is the item Besouth needs most. Besouth's leverage is the Calloway Pier Tower volume, its ongoing relationship with Meideis, and the credit support Meideis already has under the Guaranty. The client should expect Meideis to resist item 3 in particular.

**Decisions and information needed from the client:**

| # | Item | Relates to |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Expected signing and closing timetable; whether consent will be a closing condition or a deliverable; when to approach Meideis | Issue 1 |
| 2 | Whether Meideis has already been told about the sale | Issue 1 |
| 3 | Confirmation that no non-renewal notice was served | Issue 2 |
| 4 | Volume of Calloway Pier Tower glass to be delivered after February 1, 2027; whether costs can be passed through under the subcontract | Issue 2 |
| 5 | Whether Besouth wants a continuing relationship with Meideis beyond Calloway Pier Tower | Issues 2 and 3 |
| 6 | Any non-Meideis glass purchases since February 2024; other active projects using other fabricators | Issue 3 |
| 7 | Payment status and any disputed invoices with Meideis | Issue 4 |
| 8 | Any §7.2 price adjustment notices received | Issue 5 |
| 9 | Copies of the equity purchase agreement draft and the Calloway Pier Tower subcontract, neither of which is in the folder | General |

**Information gaps.** We have not seen the following, and I have not made assumptions about their contents:
- the Pellworth equity purchase agreement;
- the Tidewater Hallcroft subcontract;
- any correspondence with Meideis about renewal or the sale; and
- the insurance enclosures.

Once we have these, I can update the analysis, particularly on Issues 1 and 2.

**MEMORANDUM**

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** Associate
**Date:** November 2, 2026
**Re:** Besouth Facade Systems, Inc. / Meideis Glass Fabrication Co.: Review of supply arrangements ahead of the Pellworth transaction and Calloway Pier Tower work

---

## 1. Summary

I reviewed the five files in the matter folder:

- Glass Supply Agreement dated February 1, 2024 (the "**Supply Agreement**")
- Statement of Work No. 1 – Calloway Pier Tower dated March 18, 2024 (the "**SOW**")
- Amendment No. 1 dated June 15, 2026 (the "**Amendment**")
- Besouth Holdings LLC Parent Guaranty dated October 5, 2026 (the "**Guaranty**")
- Meideis's insurance certificate cover letter dated October 20, 2026

Two issues need attention before Besouth relies on these documents and before the Pellworth deal closes. They are listed in priority order.

1. **Change of control consent (high priority / closing item).** Pellworth's purchase of Besouth Holdings is an indirect Change of Control under the Supply Agreement. It needs Meideis's prior written consent. Without that consent, Meideis can terminate the agreement and the Calloway Pier Tower SOW on 30 days' notice.
2. **Overbroad exclusivity (high priority / commercial flexibility).** The Supply Agreement requires Besouth *and its Affiliates* to buy all of their architectural glass in North America from Meideis. That obligation overrides the SOW's narrower, project-only exclusivity. After closing it may extend to Pellworth's other portfolio companies.

The remaining points are lower priority. The insurance cover letter appears compliant. Background facts and items needing client input are collected at the end.

---

## 2. Key background terms

- **Initial Term.** The Supply Agreement took effect February 1, 2024. Under Section 2.1 it runs for three years from that date, so the Initial Term ends on or about **January 31, 2027**. The Amendment (Recital B) and the Guaranty (Recital C) both confirm this.
- **Order of precedence (Supply Agreement § 18.2).** Where the documents conflict, they prevail in this order:
  1. Amendments
  2. The Supply Agreement
  3. Any Statement of Work

  So the Supply Agreement prevails over the SOW. Amendment No. 1 is expressly an "Amendment" for this purpose (Amendment § 1.4).
- **Governing law and forum.** Delaware law governs (§ 18.6). The courts of New Castle County, Delaware have exclusive jurisdiction after an executive escalation step (§ 17).

---

## 3. Issues (in order of priority)

### Issue 1: Pellworth acquisition triggers Meideis's change of control consent and termination right

**Priority:** Highest. This affects closing and puts the Calloway Pier Tower supply at risk.

**Where:**
- Supply Agreement § 1.1 (definition of "Change of Control")
- Supply Agreement § 16.1 (consent required for any assignment)
- Supply Agreement § 16.2 (change of control treated as an assignment)
- Supply Agreement § 16.3 (Meideis's termination right)
- Guaranty § 8.2 (continuation of the Guaranty after a change of control of the Guarantor)

**What the documents say:**
- **§ 1.1.** A "Change of Control" includes any transaction in which a person acquires, directly or indirectly, more than 50% of the voting equity "of Buyer **or of any direct or indirect parent** of Buyer."
- **§ 16.2.** Any Change of Control of Besouth, "including a Change of Control occurring at the level of any direct or indirect parent of Buyer," is "**deemed an assignment**" of the agreement. It therefore requires Meideis's **prior written consent** under § 16.1. Besouth must also give Meideis written notice of the proposed Change of Control **at least 30 days before completion**.
- **§ 16.3.** If a Change of Control occurs without consent, Meideis may terminate the Supply Agreement and any or all Statements of Work on **30 days' written notice**. It may do so at any time within **12 months** after it learns of the Change of Control.
- **§ 16.1.** Any purported assignment in breach of § 16 is **void**.

**Why it matters:**
- Pellworth is buying all of the equity of Besouth Holdings LLC, which directly or indirectly owns all of Besouth (Guaranty Recital D). That is an indirect Change of Control under limb (a) of the definition.
- It does not matter that Besouth Facade Systems itself is not a party to the equity sale. The definition and § 16.2 are drafted expressly to capture parent-level transactions.
- If the deal closes without consent, Meideis would have a 12-month option to walk away from the Calloway Pier Tower SOW mid-project, on only 30 days' notice. It could also use that option as leverage to reprice.
- Besouth relies on Meideis as its exclusive source of insulated glass units for the project (SOW § 2.1). Losing Meideis mid-project would expose Besouth to:
  - delay and liquidated damages claims under its subcontract with Tidewater Hallcroft Builders;
  - re-qualification costs for a replacement fabricator, including a new mock-up, Architect of Record approvals and silicone compatibility testing under SOW §§ 3.3(d), 3.4 and 6.1.
- The "deemed assignment" also raises a void-transfer argument that Meideis could invoke.

**The Guaranty does not solve this.**
- Guaranty § 8.2 says only that Besouth Holdings "may undergo a change of control" and that the Guaranty continues to bind it afterwards.
- That language is Besouth Holdings' own covenant, given in favor of Meideis. It is not Meideis's consent under § 16.2 of the Supply Agreement and does not waive that requirement. The Guaranty does not refer to § 16 at all.
- Meideis's countersignature on the Guaranty ("Acknowledged and accepted") should not be relied on as consent. Any argument to that effect would conflict with:
  - the "prior written consent" requirement;
  - the no-waiver clause in Supply Agreement § 18.4;
  - the written-amendment requirement in § 18.3.
- Nothing else in the folder grants or waives the consent.
- Guaranty § 8.2 also creates a **separate obligation**: Besouth Holdings must notify Meideis within 10 business days after closing.

**Recommendation:**
- **Obtain Meideis's written consent before closing.** It should expressly reference §§ 16.1–16.3, consent to the Pellworth acquisition of Besouth Holdings, and waive the § 16.3 termination right for this transaction.
- **Build the consent into the Pellworth purchase agreement** as a closing condition or required closing deliverable, and list it on the required-consents disclosure schedule.
- **Calendar the pre-closing notice.** Besouth's § 16.2 notice must be given at least 30 days before the expected closing date, in the form required by § 18.1.
- **Calendar the post-closing notice.** Besouth Holdings' Guaranty § 8.2 notice is due within 10 business days after closing.
- **Use the consent request to negotiate**, if the client is willing. For example, ask Meideis to narrow the exclusivity at the same time (see Issue 2), since that discussion will be needed anyway.

**Client decision / follow-up:**
- Confirm the target signing and closing dates.
- Confirm whether anyone at Besouth has already discussed the sale with Meideis.
- Decide who will approach Meideis (Besouth management or counsel) and when.

---

### Issue 2: Supply Agreement exclusivity covers all architectural glass, North America-wide, including Affiliates, and overrides the SOW's project-only scope

**Priority:** High. This limits Besouth's commercial flexibility and may extend to Pellworth's portfolio after closing.

**Where:**
- Supply Agreement § 3.1 (exclusive purchase obligation)
- Supply Agreement § 1.1 (definition of "Affiliate")
- Supply Agreement § 18.2 (order of precedence)
- SOW § 2.1 (project exclusivity)

**What the documents say:**
- **§ 3.1** requires Besouth to purchase, and to "cause its Affiliates to" purchase, from Meideis "**all of its requirements for architectural glass products throughout North America**." Covered products include:
  - insulated glass units;
  - laminated glass;
  - heat-strengthened and tempered glass;
  - coated and spandrel glass;

  for any facade application. Besouth and its Affiliates may not buy these products from anyone else during the Term.
- **SOW § 2.1** reflects the narrower commercial deal. Meideis is Besouth's exclusive source of **insulated glass units for the Calloway Pier Tower project, Baltimore, Maryland** only.
- **§ 18.2.** The Supply Agreement prevails over any Statement of Work. The SOW therefore does not narrow § 3.1. The broader agreement-level exclusivity controls.
- **Affiliate (§ 1.1)** means any person that "now or hereafter" controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with Besouth.

**Why it matters:**
- On its face, Besouth is in breach whenever it buys any architectural glass, for any project anywhere in North America, from a supplier other than Meideis.
- I have no information on whether Besouth has been buying glass for other projects from other suppliers. If it has, there may be an existing breach that Meideis could raise. That risk would feature in diligence and in the consent negotiation.
- Because "Affiliate" includes entities that become affiliates "hereafter," after closing it may capture:
  - Besouth Holdings;
  - Pellworth;
  - every Pellworth portfolio company under common control.

  Any of those companies that buys facade glass in North America could put Besouth in breach. Besouth also cannot realistically "cause" Pellworth's other portfolio companies to comply. This is likely to be a significant diligence concern for Pellworth.
- Besouth also loses pricing leverage. It cannot competitively bid glass on other projects, and its only price protection is the PPI-based cap in § 7.2.
- Breach would expose Besouth to:
  - termination for material breach under § 15.1, which could reach the Calloway Pier Tower SOW;
  - damages claims for lost volume. The § 11.1 exclusion of consequential damages and lost profits may limit these, but direct lost-margin damages could still be argued.

**Recommendation:**
- **Negotiate an amendment to § 3.1** that limits exclusivity to the SOW scope: insulated glass units for the Calloway Pier Tower project. Alternatively, limit it to products and projects that Besouth elects to place under a Statement of Work.
- **Remove the obligation to "cause its Affiliates" to purchase from Meideis.** At a minimum, carve out Besouth's parents and any entity under common control with Besouth through a private equity sponsor, including Pellworth and its portfolio companies.
- **Document the change as an Amendment** signed under § 18.3, so that it sits at the top of the § 18.2 hierarchy. Ideally, sign it together with the change of control consent in Issue 1.
- **Assess past compliance.** Ask the client whether it has sourced glass elsewhere since February 2024. If it has, consider seeking a release from Meideis covering past purchases in the same amendment.

**Client decision / follow-up:**

- Decide how much exclusivity Besouth is willing to offer Meideis in exchange for consent and narrowing. For example, it could offer volume commitments or right-of-first-offer on future bids instead of full exclusivity.

### Issue 3: Other points to note (lower priority)

**(a) Liability cap is set per SOW (Supply Agreement § 11.2).**
- Each party's liability under a Statement of Work is capped at the amounts paid and payable under that SOW, except for indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct.
- Removal and reinstallation reimbursement under § 9.4 is also subject to this cap.
- For Calloway Pier Tower, the estimated SOW value is about 186,000 sq. ft. at roughly $27–$46 per sq. ft. (about $5.5 million). The cap is probably adequate for most warranty exposure.
- However, seal failures could appear across many units years into the 10-year seal warranty (§ 9.2). Removal and reinstallation on a 31-story tower is expensive.
- **Recommendation:** No immediate action. Besouth should compare this cap with the warranty and back-charge obligations it owes Tidewater and the Owner under its subcontract. If there is a gap, raise it in any amendment negotiation.

**(b) Guaranty: Besouth Holdings' exposure and post-closing position.**
- The Guaranty covers payment obligations only (§ 2.3). It is capped at **$4,500,000** plus enforcement costs (§ 3).
- It continues through a change of control of Besouth Holdings (§ 8.2). Pellworth will therefore inherit a contingent liability at the holding level. It should be disclosed in the Pellworth transaction.
- Under § 8.3, Besouth Holdings may terminate the Guaranty for future obligations if it ceases to own a majority of Besouth. That will not happen in this deal, because Holdings keeps Besouth.
- **Recommendation:** Disclose the Guaranty to Pellworth. Confirm whether Pellworth expects the Guaranty to remain in place or to be replaced.

**(c) Purchase Order formalities (SOW § 9.1; Supply Agreement §§ 4.2, 4.3).**
- Each Calloway Pier Tower Purchase Order must reference "SOW No. 1 – Calloway Pier Tower."
- Meideis has 5 business days to accept or reject a Purchase Order.
- **Recommendation:** Make sure Besouth's project team is following these steps. They protect Besouth's position on lead times and remakes.

**(d) Insurance certificate cover letter (no issue identified).**
- The October 20, 2026 letter delivers renewal certificates under § 13.2 for the October 1, 2026 to October 1, 2027 policy year.
- The stated limits and A.M. Best ratings meet or exceed the § 13.1 minimums.
- Besouth and its Affiliates are named as additional insureds on the commercial general liability and umbrella policies, on a primary and non-contributory basis, covering completed operations.
- **Recommendation:** No action needed beyond the following:
  - Have someone check the enclosed ACORD 25 and endorsements against the letter. We have only the cover letter, not the enclosures.
  - If Besouth's subcontract requires it, ask the broker (Andrea Voss) for a separate project certificate naming the Owner, Tidewater and the Architect of Record.
